description: Find places (POIs) along a route with the REAL extra travel time of stopping at each — never a straight-line guess. Provide `origin` + `destination` (a route is computed) or an existing route's `geometry_polyline6`, plus a free-text `query` ("coffee", "EV charger", "truck stop") and `max_detour_minutes` (default 10). For a category intent ("fuel", "EV charger", "coffee") pass `category` instead of relying on words alone: it takes the same vocabulary as `nearby_places` (lowercased OSM tag values such as "fuel", "cafe", "charging_station", "parking", "pharmacy"), and common colloquial phrases are normalised server-side ("petrol station" and "gas station" to fuel, "coffee" to cafe, "EV charger" to charging_station). `query` alone also promotes a pure category phrase to the same browse, so "fuel" finds fuel stations rather than places whose NAME starts "Ful"; anything else stays free-text name matching. When a browse ran, the response echoes the tokens used in `matched_categories`. Candidates near the route corridor are priced through the routing engine with your costing: detour = (origin→place) + (place→destination) − (origin→destination). Costing "auto", "truck" (with a `truck` profile the detours respect dimensional/ADR restrictions), "bicycle", "pedestrian" or "motor_scooter". Returns results sorted by detour with detour_minutes, detour_km, along_route_position (0-1) and off_route_m; at most 25 candidates are priced per call (candidate_cap).

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description:
Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

TruckSpec.description:
Truck profile for routing: physical dimensions plus the ADR
dangerous-goods declaration. Omitted dimensions default to the EU
maximum authorised dimensions of Council Directive 96/53/EC (4.0 m
height, 2.55 m width, 16.5 m length, 40 t gross weight).

gross_weight_t.description: Gross combination weight in metric tonnes.

hazmat.description:
Whether the vehicle carries dangerous goods (ADR). Defaults to
false.

tunnel_code.description:
ADR 8.6.4 tunnel restriction code of the load, e.g. "B", "C5000D",
"B/D", or "(—)"/"none" for explicitly unrestricted. Leave unset if
unknown: a hazmat load without a code is conservatively treated as
code B (allowed only through category-A tunnels).

category.description:
Explicit place category ("fuel", "cafe", "charging_station" — same
vocabulary as nearby_places). Colloquial phrases are normalised
server-side; prefer this over query for category intents.

costing.description:
Costing model for the route and detour matrix: "auto" (default),
"truck", "bicycle", "pedestrian" or "motor_scooter".

geometry_polyline6.description:
An existing route geometry as an encoded polyline6 (the `route`
tool's `geometry_polyline6`). Provide either this or `origin` +
`destination`, not both.

max_detour_minutes.description: Largest acceptable detour in minutes (default 10, at most 120).

origin.description: Route origin (with `destination`, when no geometry is given).

query.description: Free-text POI query, e.g. "coffee", "EV charger", "truck stop".

truck.description:
Truck profile (dimensions + ADR declaration). Requires costing
"truck"; the detours then respect dimensional/ADR restrictions.

name: search_along_route

AlongRouteHit.description: One place found along the route, with its honest detour cost.

along_route_position.description:
Where along the route the place sits, 0.0 (origin) to 1.0
(destination), by distance along the geometry.

detour_km.description:
Extra travel distance in kilometres, when the engine reported
distances.

detour_minutes.description:
Extra travel time of visiting this place, in minutes (rounded to
0.1): (origin→place) + (place→destination) − (origin→destination),
all computed by the routing engine with the request's costing.

detour_s.description: The same detour in raw seconds.

fuel_brand.description:
The matched fuel station's brand, when known (same conditions as
`fuel_prices`).

fuel_prices.description:
Live pump prices for this fuel/petrol station, keyed by fuel code
(e.g. "diesel", "petrol_95"), each `{value, currency, updated_at}`.
Only ever present when the server is gateway-preferred AND the
deployment configured `SN_FUEL_PRICES` AND this result matched a
station within range — never fabricated. Direct-backend fallback
never sets this (see the gap this closes in the PR description).

fuel_updated_at.description:
When the matched fuel station's prices were last refreshed (RFC
3339), when known (same conditions as `fuel_prices`).

off_route_m.description: Straight-line distance from the place to the route, metres.

place.description: The place (geocoder hit: name, label, coordinates, type).

label.description: Human-readable one-line label assembled from the address parts.

match.description:
How far this hit can be trusted to be the place that was asked
for — see [`GeocodeMatch`]. Present whenever the MapMap gateway
answered; absent on a deployment falling back to the direct Photon
geocoder, and absent on the gateway's own fast paths (a pasted
coordinate pair, a bare UK outward code, a category browse), which
answer without a ranking to report on.

name.description: Place name, when the source feature has one.

type.description:
Feature type, e.g. "house", "street", "city" (falls back to the
OSM value when the endpoint does not classify).

GeocodeMatch.description:
How well one geocoding result answers what was actually asked.

Geocoding's real failure mode is not "no answer" but a confident answer
to a different question: a plausible row on the wrong street, with
nothing in the response to say so. This object is that missing say-so,
and an agent should read it before acting on an address.

How to read it:

* Any component `unmatched` or `inferred` on the TOP hit means the
  answer does not carry the address that was asked for — an `unmatched`
  postcode means the result has no postcode at all, `inferred` means it
  has a different one. Neither is a match. Say so rather than presenting
  the hit as the address, and reach for `verify_places` when the address
  came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using.
* A small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose between this hit
  and the runner-up, which is exactly when to show the alternatives
  instead of picking one for the user.

components.description:
Per-component verdict on this hit: one entry for each structured
component supplied, and empty when the query was free text only.

score_gap.description:
The top result's score minus the runner-up's, rounded to 3 decimal
places. `0` for a single result, and `0` from the `photon` source,
which publishes no per-result score — so a `0` is "no signal", not
"a tie".

source.description:
Which backend answered: "mapmap-index" (the first-party index) or
"photon".

GeocodeMatchComponents.description:
Per-component verdicts inside a [`GeocodeMatch`]. Each is one of
"matched", "inferred" or "unmatched"; a component that was not supplied
is absent entirely.

* "matched" — the result's own field carries the value asked for (case-
  and accent-insensitive, and by containment, so `city: "London"`
  matches "City of London").
* "inferred" — the result carries a value for that component, but not
  the one asked for. It reached the page through ranking, as when a
  street is found by its transliterated name and displayed under its
  canonical one.
* "unmatched" — the result carries no value for that component at all.

candidate_cap.description: The matrix fan-out cap in force.

candidates_considered.description: Candidates found near the corridor before pricing.

candidates_costed.description:
Candidates actually priced through the engine (fan-out is capped
at `candidate_cap` nearest-to-route).

costing.description: The costing the detours were priced with.

fuel_attribution.description:
Attribution string for fuel-price data sources, present only when
at least one returned result carries `fuel_prices` (gateway-preferred
mode with `SN_FUEL_PRICES` configured; see [`AlongRouteHit`]).

matched_categories.description:
The normalised category tokens the candidates were browsed by,
present only when a category browse actually ran (an explicit
`category`, or a query the server promoted to one). Absent means
free-text name matching answered the call, so a caller can tell how
its words were understood rather than inferring it from the results.

results.description: Places within the detour budget, cheapest detour first.

route_duration_s.description:
Direct origin→destination travel time in seconds (same estimator
as the detour legs), when routable.

route_length_m.description: Length of the route geometry in metres.
